Kyle — appreciate the clarity. High level attached is a one-page MAP and a proposed acceptance-test-suite. Key highlights below; full details in attachments (MAP_v2.xlsx, acceptance-test-suite.md).

Anchor metrics (recommended):
- Latency: P95 <= 180ms (prompt length median 120 tokens)
- Availability: 99.5% during working hours (US-PT window)
- Unit cost: <= $0.85 per 1k tokens (after recommended batching/quantization)
- Accuracy: Entity extraction F1 >= 0.88 on MedShift anonymized sample
- Stability: No more than 3 model-level regressions in 2-week run (concordance checks)

Acceptance tests (high level):
- Smoke: basic generation + response schema validation (30s)
- Latency sweep: 500 concurrent short requests (track P50/P95/P99)
- Cost simulation: synthetic token mix to estimate unit cost
- Accuracy run: run MedShift extraction tests and compute F1/precision/recall
- Fault injection: degrade instance and verify fallback to warm model variant

Exit gates / fail rules:
- Immediate fail: Accuracy < 0.82 OR P95 > 400ms for a sustained hour
- Soft fail (requires remediation plan): Unit cost > $1.10 OR >5% request errors across 24h

Proposed timeline (two-week evaluation):
- Week 0 (next 3 business days): onboarding + shared test artifacts
- Week 1: smoke + latency & accuracy baseline runs
- Week 2: production-like throughput + fault injection + signoff window

Security gating: we will provide SOC2 attestation doc and reviewer access to relevant logs (read-only). I flagged procurement items for Ben to confirm.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP timeline + owners), acceptance-test-suite.md (test descriptions + command-line examples)

If that looks ok I can lock in the pilot slot for June 1 — please confirm by Tuesday EOD.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Kyle / Sean — quick follow up with a few concrete pass/fail numbers and observability hooks we recommend the MedShift QA run. I focused on tests that are lightweight but tell an engineer whether to stop the run early.

Pass/fail clarifications (suggested):
- Latency: P95 target 180ms, green; 180–300ms = amber (requires ramp-down of batch size); >300ms = red (stop long runs, investigate kernel selection).
- Accuracy: F1 >= 0.88 = green; 0.85–0.88 = amber (need per-intent analysis); <0.85 = red (halt close path).
- Error rate: <0.5% = green; 0.5–2% = amber; >2% = red.

Observability hooks for each test:
- Correlate model variant + instance id + request id.
- Attach sample failing inputs to the accuracy report (s3 link).
- Record KV-cache hit rates for prefix-heavy workflows (helps explain latency variance).

Quick note on acceptance tests: I trimmed the suite to a 45-minute run that still covers: smoke, latency sweep, accuracy, and a short fault injection. See acceptance-test-suite.md for commands.

I'll be available tomorrow to walk QA through the commands if useful.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
